Hyperparameter Tuning for Imputation Methods

Source: R/tune_imp.R
tune_imp.Rd

Tune method-specific hyperparameters by repeatedly masking observed values, imputing them, and comparing the imputed values with the original values.

Usage

tune_imp(
  obj,
  parameters = NULL,
  .f,
  na_loc = NULL,
  num_na = NULL,
  n_reps = 1,
  n_cols = NULL,
  n_rows = 2,
  rowmax = 0.9,
  colmax = 0.9,
  na_col_subset = NULL,
  max_attempts = 100,
  .progress = TRUE,
  cores = 1,
  location = NULL,
  pin_blas = TRUE
)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix.

parameters

A data frame or NULL. One row per parameter set, one column per argument of .f other than obj. List-columns hold arguments that are not scalars. Duplicate rows are removed. NULL is allowed only for a custom .f, which is then called with its defaults.

.f

Character or function. One of "knn_imp", "pca_imp", or "slide_imp", or a custom imputation function, as described in Details.

na_loc

A matrix, numeric vector, list, or NULL. Positions to mask in place of sampled ones. A two-column matrix holds row and column indices, a numeric vector holds linear positions, and a list holds one of those per repetition.

num_na

Integer or NULL. Total number of missing values per repetition. When given, n_cols is ignored and the values are spread as evenly as possible over num_na %/% n_rows columns.

n_reps

Integer. Number of independent repetitions.

n_cols

Integer or NULL. Number of columns that receive missing values.

n_rows

Integer. Minimum number of missing values per selected column.

rowmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Maximum proportion of missing values per row after injection.

colmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Maximum proportion of missing values per column after injection.

na_col_subset

Optional character or integer vector. The columns that can receive missing values, by name or by number.

max_attempts

Integer. Maximum number of sampling attempts per repetition before an error.

.progress

Logical. If TRUE, show progress during tuning.

cores

Integer. Number of cores for K-NN imputation, including slide_imp() with k. For other methods, use mirai::daemons().

location

Numeric or NULL. The position of each column of obj, sorted in ascending order. .f = "slide_imp" needs it, and the other methods ignore it.

pin_blas

Logical. If TRUE, pin BLAS threads to 1 on the mirai daemons in a parallel run. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

A data frame of class slideimp_tune with these columns:

  • the columns of parameters.

  • param_set, an integer ID for each unique parameter combination.

  • rep_id, an integer repetition index.

  • result, a list-column of data frames, each with truth and estimate columns.

  • error, a character column with the error message of a failed iteration, or NA.

Details

A custom .f must accept obj as its first argument and return a numeric matrix with the same dimensions as obj and no Inf values. tune_imp() calls it once with the first parameter set before tuning starts, and stops if that call fails. After that, an iteration that fails or breaks this rule is recorded in the error column.

The columns of parameters for a custom function must not use the names of the columns that tune_imp() and compute_metrics() add: param_set, rep_id, result, error, n, n_miss, .metric, .estimator, and .estimate.

When mirai daemons are set, a custom function runs on the daemons. It finds the packages attached on the daemons, but not the variables of the session that defined it. Pass such values through parameters.

When mirai daemons are set, each daemon receives one copy of obj before tuning starts and keeps it until tuning ends. Each iteration masks cells in a second copy. Memory use therefore grows with the number of daemons.

When na_loc is supplied, num_na, n_reps, n_cols, n_rows, rowmax, colmax, na_col_subset, and max_attempts are ignored. The positions are not checked against rowmax or colmax.

When .f is a character string, columns in parameters are validated against the selected method:

  • "knn_imp" requires k.

  • "pca_imp" requires ncp.

  • "slide_imp" requires window_size, overlap_size, and min_window_n, plus exactly one of k or ncp.

To tune parameters for grouped imputation, tune knn_imp() or pca_imp() on representative groups, then pass the selected parameters to group_imp().

The top-level rowmax and colmax arguments control random missing-value injection performed by sample_na_loc(). To tune or pass an imputation method's own colmax argument, include a colmax column in parameters.

Tuning results can be summarized with compute_metrics() or evaluated with external packages such as yardstick.

Missing values and non-finite input

obj must be a double matrix. An integer or logical matrix is rejected, not converted. Convert one with storage.mode(obj) <- "double".

NA and NaN are both treated as missing. The package does not distinguish between them.

Inf and -Inf are rejected on entry, and so is a column with no observed values (every cell NA or NaN). Locate them with which(is.infinite(obj), arr.ind = TRUE) and which(colSums(!is.na(obj)) == 0).

Parallelization

  • K-NN: use the cores argument. If mirai daemons are active, cores is set to 1 to avoid nested parallelism.

  • PCA: use mirai::daemons() instead of cores.

  • With mirai daemons, each daemon runs BLAS on one thread unless pin_blas = FALSE.

PCA Performance tips

Three arguments set the speed: solver, threshold, and scale. Tune these first, then the accuracy arguments ncp and coeff.ridge, on a representative subset.

Exact vs. LOBPCG. "lobpcg" suits large, approximately low-rank matrices with small ncp. "exact" suits small matrices, such as slide_imp() windows, where it is faster. It is also more reliable: it always converges, to eigenvectors exact to machine precision, while LOBPCG stops at the tolerance set in lobpcg_control() and can take many iterations, or reach maxiter, when the eigenvalues around the ncp-th one are close together. The warm start makes each later LOBPCG solve cheap: pca_imp() starts LOBPCG from the previous eigenblock and search direction, so once the imputed values stabilize, each solve takes a few iterations. The gain grows with the number of EM iterations, whatever the rank. solver = "auto", the default, chooses between the two and is a safe start.

Threshold. The default 1e-6 is conservative. 1e-5 is often faster and gives very similar values.

Scale. For columns on a common scale, such as DNA methylation beta values in [0, 1], scale = FALSE can be faster and more accurate.

BLAS. On Windows, the BLAS that ships with R can be slow, and OpenBLAS can replace it.

See Speeding up PCA imputation for the full workflow.

See also

sample_na_loc() to draw the na_loc locations in advance.

Examples

set.seed(123)

# Simulate some data
obj <- sim_mat(10, 50)$input

# Tune K-NN imputation with random missing-value injection.
# Use larger `num_na` and `n_reps` values for real analyses.
params_knn <- data.frame(k = c(2, 4))
results <- tune_imp(
  obj,
  params_knn,
  .f = "knn_imp",
  n_reps = 1,
  num_na = 10,
  .progress = FALSE
)
#> Tuning `knn_imp()`
#> Step 1/2: Resolving NA locations
#> Running mode: sequential
#> Step 2/2: Tuning
compute_metrics(results)
#>   k param_set rep_id error  n n_miss .metric .estimator .estimate
#> 1 2         1      1  <NA> 10      0     mae   standard 0.1735950
#> 2 2         1      1  <NA> 10      0    rmse   standard 0.2306389
#> 3 4         2      1  <NA> 10      0     mae   standard 0.2173526
#> 4 4         2      1  <NA> 10      0    rmse   standard 0.2634978

# Tune with fixed missing-value positions
na_positions <- list(
  matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 1), ncol = 2),
  matrix(c(2, 3, 4, 2, 2, 2), ncol = 2)
)

results_fixed <- tune_imp(
  obj,
  data.frame(k = 2),
  .f = "knn_imp",
  na_loc = na_positions,
  .progress = FALSE
)
#> Tuning `knn_imp()`
#> Step 1/2: Resolving NA locations
#> Running mode: sequential
#> Step 2/2: Tuning

# Custom imputation function
custom_fill <- function(obj, val = 0) {
  obj[is.na(obj)] <- val
  obj
}

tune_imp(
  obj,
  data.frame(val = c(0, 1)),
  .f = custom_fill,
  num_na = 10,
  .progress = FALSE
)
#> Tuning a custom function
#> Step 1/2: Resolving NA locations
#> Running mode: sequential
#> Step 2/2: Tuning
#> # slideimp table: 2 x 5
#>  val param_set rep_id        result error
#>    0         1      1 <df [10 x 2]>  <NA>
#>    1         2      1 <df [10 x 2]>  <NA>

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("mirai", quietly = TRUE)
# Parallel tuning with mirai
mirai::daemons(2)

parameters_custom <- data.frame(mean = c(0, 1), sd = c(1, 1))

custom_imp <- function(obj, mean, sd) {
  na_pos <- is.na(obj)
  obj[na_pos] <- stats::rnorm(sum(na_pos), mean = mean, sd = sd)
  obj
}

results_p <- tune_imp(
  obj,
  parameters_custom,
  .f = custom_imp,
  n_reps = 1,
  num_na = 10,
  .progress = FALSE
)

mirai::daemons(0)
}
